title: Reverse Linked List
statement: You get the first node of a singly linked list. Reverse the list so the arrows point the other way, and return the new first node. The list may be empty.

example.caption: Same nodes, arrows flipped. The old tail 4 becomes the new head.

idea.sentence: Walk the list once and turn each node's arrow around, but save the next node before you cut the link.

jargon.plain: Nodes that each hold a value and one pointer to the next node. You can only walk forward.

watch.inputHint: One argument: the node values in order, e.g. [1,2,3]

compare.bruteLabel: Copy values to an array, write them back reversed

rows.name: Copy to an array
rows.note: Two passes and a side array that holds every value.

rows.name: Flip pointers in place
rows.note: One pass. Only three pointers: prev, cur and next.

fast.takeaway: Both are one pass. Flipping the arrows needs no extra memory, because the list itself becomes the answer.

stages.title: Set up prev and cur
stages.note: prev is the reversed part, empty at first. cur is the node about to be flipped, the head.

stages.title: Save next
stages.note: Remember cur.next. After the flip the old link is gone, so this is the only way to the rest.

stages.title: Flip the arrow
stages.note: Point cur at prev instead of at the next node.

stages.title: Step forward
stages.note: cur joins the reversed part (prev = cur). Then cur moves to the saved next.

stages.title: Return prev
stages.note: When cur runs off the end, prev is the old tail and the new head.

edges.title: Empty list
edges.why: The loop never runs and prev is still null. Returning prev is correct.

edges.title: One node
edges.why: One flip: the node points at null, which it already did.

edges.title: Repeated values
edges.why: Equal values are fine. You reverse nodes, not values.

edges.title: Long list
edges.why: The loop is not recursive, so a long list cannot overflow the call stack.

gotchas.text: Save cur.next before cur.next = prev. Do it in the other order and the rest of the list is lost.
Return prev, not cur. When the loop ends cur is null.
Declare prev as ListNode | null. Plain let prev = null makes TypeScript infer the type null and reject the assignment later.
var prev *ListNode starts as nil, which is exactly the empty reversed list. Do not allocate a dummy node for it.
Build nodes with next: null, not undefined. A loop that tests cur !== null would never stop on a node whose next is undefined.

recap.key: Walk once. For each node save next, point it backwards, then move forward. Return prev.
moves: Advance prev and cur. Return prev at the end
